about: How nations are placed on the map and how their starting land grows. Used by src/game/territory.ts and src/ui/placement.ts.

europe.name: Europe
europe.about: Where nations may be placed for the Europe test. A rough outline as [longitude, latitude] points (east and north are positive). It follows the middle of the Mediterranean and the Black Sea, so North Africa and Anatolia stay out.

start.about: Where 'Surprise me' and Fill put nations. coastPreference: how often (0 to 1) they pick a spot next to the sea, a lake or a river while there is one with room. The water closes off one side, so nations don't snake out in every direction, and the inland gaps left between them are filled by later nations. They also never start a nation in a free pocket of land smaller than minGap km², or in a pocket surrounded by only one nation (an enclave) smaller than enclaveArea km²; those pockets go to the nation around them at the end of a fill. Clicking by hand can go anywhere.

fill.about: The 'Fill' testing button rolls and places nations until 'percent' of the region's land is owned (100 = until no gap is left with room for a nation of at least 'minArea' km²). It also stops after maxNations nations or maxAttempts tries. At the end of a 100% fill, the leftover land (small islands, slivers between borders) goes to the nearest nations: each spreads 'absorbSteps' pixels into it at a time (across water too, to reach islands), repeated while that still takes land; far-off islands then go to the nearest nation.

growth.about: Starting land grows out from the chosen spot, always taking the cheapest pixel it can reach next, until it has the rolled area. 'cost' is how hard each terrain is to take (plains = 1). Sea, lakes and ice can't be taken; neither can another nation's land. Rivers can be taken but cost a lot, so they tend to become borders. 'wobble' makes some areas randomly cheaper or dearer (0 = perfect blobs), so borders look natural. Afterwards 1-pixel strings are trimmed and free pockets of up to 'holeSize' pixels inside a nation are filled in (adding at most a tenth of its size).

colors.about: Each nation's colour (its flag for now), used in this order. Picked to stand out from the terrain and from each other.
